text:
marco: Quick sprint: product wants a razor-short battlecard + two landing copy variants for the launch blog/webinar. Focus: how we beat cloud-managed endpoints, simple LLM APIs, and DIY infra on production economics + reliability. Can we ship by tomorrow noon?

rina: Yep. Plan: 1) 1-page battlecard (talking points + 3 objection handlers), 2) two 2-line landing variants, 3) three subject lines for email A/B.

devin: Adding: include 1 slide with demo notes (canary rollout + fallback) and a tiny benchmark blurb. Keep everything customer-obsessed: "what does this mean for my app?"

p.j.: Bench numbers (internal quick run, 99th pct tail, 4k tokens):
- Redwood Dedicated (pinned): 95ms
- CloudY Managed Endpoint: 190ms
- Generic API Vendor: 320ms
- DIY multi-tenant infra: 430ms
footnote: sample inputs; don't claim parity across all model sizes.

kara: For the battlecard top line ideas: 
- Headline claim (not price-focused): "Predictable inference economics for production LLMs"
- Supporting bullets: 
  * Unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private = single dev surface
  * Routing + fallback keep apps online when models degrade
  * Ops controls (canary, prefix caching, autoscale) reduce regression risk and engineering toil

marco: Good. Rina, can you write the objection handlers? Keep them short, punchy.

rina: Sure. Three high-level objections and responses: 
1) "Cloud provider already offers managed endpoints" -> "True. Fast to start. Redwood reduces surprise spend and provides fallbacks so your customer-facing features stay live during model incidents."
2) "LLM APIs are simplest" -> "Great for prototypes. For production, you need rollout controls, caching, and consistent latency—Redwood's runtime and routing give you those without rebuilding infra."
3) "We self-host to control costs" -> "Self-host saves on hosting fees but increases ops burden. Redwood Private blends control with a managed control plane to cut ops tax."

marketing-bot: reminder: legal review required if we name competitors. Use anonymized labels (CloudY, API-V, DIY-Infra) unless legal signs off.

devin: Landing copy variants: 
Variant A (operator-first): "Stop guessing inference costs. Redwood gives predictable latency, caching, and rollout controls so teams ship LLM features with SLAs, not guesswork."
Variant B (product-first): "Ship delightful AI features without downtime. One API, federated runtime, and automatic fallbacks protect your users when models stutter."

marco: Nice. Email subject candidates for A/B: 
- S1: "See inference that behaves like a production system"
- S2: "Benchmarked: lower tail latency, predictable spend"
- S3: "How teams avoid model-outage surprises"

p.j.: Demo checklist for webinar: 
- Models: small chat, medium open model, RAG search
- Canary: roll out 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring alerts visible
- Fallback: switch to cheaper model variant on increased latency or errors
- Metric panels: 95/99 latency, token cost estimate, request success rate

rina: Inbound routing suggestion: tag "launch-bench" -> immediate nurture: 1) send one-pager + short benchmark highlights 2) 48h follow-up with on-demand demo video 3) qualify for SDR if > X tokens/mo in sample data. Add a checkbox: regulated industry -> offer Private brief.

kara: Slide visual notes: one bar chart of 99th-pct latency (Redwood vs CloudY vs API-V vs DIY), a tiny cost-per-1M token estimate row, and a simple flow graphic showing fallback routing. No competitor logos.

legal-bot: quick check: avoid naming real competitor products. Also avoid absolute cost claims. Methodology note required for bench slide.

marco: Timeline: 
- by 3pm today: rina battlecard draft + objection handlers; p.j. benchmark snippet; devin demo checklist
- by tomorrow 11am: kara landing copy + slides mock; marketing-bot to queue emails
- tomorrow noon: final review

devin: I'll record a 3-min demo clip for the follow-up nurture. Keep it scripted: show canary, trigger failover, show no-blip for users.

rina: Battlecard top lines (short): 
- "Production-first inference: predictable latency and spend"
- "Unified runtime across environments: same API, same controls"
- "Built-in safety for availability: canaries + fallbacks that ship with your app"

marco: Perfect. Last ask: don't use "cheaper" as the headline. Frame as "better unit economics & predictable spend". Also save assets in /marketing/webinar/prelaunch/ and add to the shared Notion page.

marketing-bot: booked workspace and Notion doc created: "Launch - inference economics". Reminder set for tomorrow noon review.

marco: Thanks team. Ping when drafts up.
